mission: HEADROOM PHASE-4 - VERIFICATION-AWARE RUNTIME GATE, MIGRATION STEP 3: MATCHER + VERIFICATION DOMINANCE (first intentional runtime behaviour change)

whatWasBuilt.gateModule: lib/contract-model/runtime/verification-gate.ts - the ONE module that owns the runtime semantics. Exports: checkIdentity, interpretVerificationStatus, assessUnit, blocksUnit, blocksNode, blocksNodeIn, incompleteDiagnostic, verificationBlocksIn, verificationIncompleteIn, VERIFICATION_DOMINANCE, capacityVerificationFloor, entryHasVerificationBlock, entryHasIncompleteVerification. Pure; no clock, no I/O, no model.
whatWasBuilt.predicate: a MATERIAL finding x its scope relation to the node being evaluated. Status is never the predicate.
whatWasBuilt.blocksUnit: REQUIRE with no record; identity mismatch on any KNOWN field; a UNIT-scoped MATERIAL finding; two records claiming one unit (AMBIGUOUS_UNIT_RECORD, fail closed). Never: REVIEW_REQUIRED / VERIFICATION_INCOMPLETE / VERIFICATION_FAILED status alone, or a NODE finding elsewhere in the unit.
whatWasBuilt.blocksNode: blocksUnit, else exact exprId membership in the unit's NODE findings. No fuzzy match, no path parsing, no array positions. Envelope precedence UNIT > NODE > none.
whatWasBuilt.identityCheckFirst: the record's identity is compared to what the runtime KNOWS (evaluateRule / 4C / 4D supply the full trio from the IR object; a bare evaluateExpression may know only the id + company/instrument). Only known fields are compared and the check records which - a partial comparison is stated, not hidden. Mismatch -> UNIT fail-closed naming the fields; NODE findings on a stale record are never salvaged.
whatWasBuilt.weakIdentity: MATERIAL findings on a WEAK-matched unit block. No findings under WEAK creates no positive claim: the runtime emits no 'verified' status anywhere (asserted by test).
whatWasBuilt.policy: DEFAULT_VERIFICATION_POLICY = ALLOW_MISSING. REQUIRE is live only when a caller states it: a unit with no record fails closed (REQUIRED_VERIFICATION_MISSING); an expression with no unit identity at all under REQUIRE also fails closed; REQUIRE reaches referenced units (a verified rule expanding an unverified definition fails at the definition). No product caller, no global default, no fixture sets REQUIRE.

fourSites.4A_nodeEntry: evaluate-expression.ts Evaluator.evaluate: order is unit -> verification gate -> memo -> (sufficiency, inside expansion) -> dispatch. A refused node returns AMBIGUOUS, value null, diagnostic MATERIAL_VERIFICATION_FINDING carrying the structured VerificationBlock; its operands are never dispatched, so the disputed literal never reaches arithmetic. The owner changes on expansion (evalDefinition / evalRuleCapacity assess the referenced unit against ITS identity, refuse at the reference node on a UNIT block, then evaluate its body under its unitId).
fourSites.4A_memoKey: exprIds are content-derived, so the same literal in two units shares an exprId. When the gate is active the memo key is prefixed with the owning unitId; when inactive the key is unchanged (inertness). Pinned by a test in which rule A and definition B carry the same exprId and only one is blocked.
fourSites.4A_wholeRule: rule-evaluator.ts: `blocked = blockedBySufficiency || blocksUnit(...) !== null`; a UNIT refusal leaves capacity and conditions unevaluated with a note naming the reason and adds `verificationBlock` to the RuleEvaluation (present only when refused). NODE findings stay node-local.
fourSites.4A_incomplete: an informational diagnostic VERIFICATION_INCOMPLETE (status EXECUTABLE) is recorded once on entry to a unit whose status is VERIFICATION_INCOMPLETE / VERIFICATION_FAILED / unrecognized. It nulls nothing.
fourSites.4C_dominance: capacity/state.ts: VERIFICATION_DOMINANCE (defined in the gate module, re-exported beside SUFFICIENCY_DOMINANCE, NOT merged). The floor is read AFTER evaluating the capacity-driving expression, from the rule's own assessment plus every block/incompleteness the evaluator actually hit (including inside expanded units). Floors fold into the existing worst-of over CAPACITY_STATUS_PRECEDENCE with the sufficiency floor; legalUnsafe withholds published amounts and reports arithmetic under `provisional` exactly as sufficiency does.
fourSites.4C_pools: a shared-capacity cap is not a verifiable unit; its expansions are still gated, and under REQUIRE the pool itself fails closed (no unit can vouch for it). A refusal inside a pool is reported as PHASE3_VERIFICATION_MATERIAL_FINDING, never as an ambiguous financial fact.
fourSites.4D_legalFloor: transaction/simulate.ts beside unsafeLegal: blocksUnit on each selected rule makes every condition REVIEW_REQUIRED (same shape as unsafeLegal) and records the limitation once per rule; a NODE refusal inside a condition's expression makes that condition REVIEW_REQUIRED (not AMBIGUOUS) with the limitation; the three evaluateCapacityState calls and the condition evaluations receive the envelope and policy. consumptionResult carries PHASE3_VERIFICATION_MATERIAL_FINDING / PHASE3_VERIFICATION_INCOMPLETE from the entry and floors the draw outcome to REVIEW_REQUIRED (a refused capacity's INDETERMINATE becomes REVIEW_REQUIRED; a definite negative stands). SIMULATION_FLOOR maps both codes to REVIEW_REQUIRED.
fourSites.4D_atomicity: preserved by construction - no new write path. Pinned: pre-state, ledger and graph byte-identical after simulation; preTransactionState.stateHash unchanged; commitPlan.committable false; the refused figure never appears in the result.

vocabularyAdded.whyTheDisclosedAdditions: §25 and success-gate §32.8 require VERIFICATION_INCOMPLETE to stay DISTINGUISHABLE from a material defect at every layer, and §15 floors it at REVIEW_REQUIRED. Reusing PHASE3_VERIFICATION_MATERIAL_FINDING for an incomplete verification would label 'the verifier ran out of evidence' as 'a material finding exists', which is the exact conflation the design forbids. These are CODES, not statuses; no runtime status was added (§18's core rule). The structured refusal (VerificationBlock: reason, scope, unitId, exprId, findingIds, mismatches, identityStrength) rides on the diagnostic as an optional `verification` field and on limitation messages as a `[REASON]` prefix, so the authorized code stays the code and the reason stays machine-readable.

unitBlockFalsePositiveInspection.method: every one of the 30 UNIT blocks in the bindable set classified deterministically by resolver cause, then read by hand (reason excerpts are in the probe artifact)
unitBlockFalsePositiveInspection.reading: None of the 30 is benign: each names an operative defect - a missing proviso or cap, a carve-out the IR drops, a fabricated threshold, twelve LTV percentages absent from the IR, an entity scope narrower than the source, a second prohibited act the rule omits. The pressure is OVER-BREADTH, not false positives: in roughly 21 of 30 the verifier's path text names a sub-part (a condition, a gatedBy, one operand) that the resolver could not bind, so one clause's defect disables the whole unit. The 4 WRONG_ENTITY_SCOPE and 2 MISSING_RULE blocks are unit-level defects by nature and UNIT is the correct scope, not over-broad. Fail-closed behaviour was not weakened to improve any count.
unitBlockFalsePositiveInspection.whereThePressureWouldBeRelieved: on the Phase-3 side, by having the verifier emit exact paths (or exprIds) for the sub-part it names - not by loosening the runtime matcher.
